finding: CNN activation memory scales approximately linearly with batch size.
evidence: At image size 224, increasing batch size from 1 to 8 increased analytical activation memory by 8.00x.
why_it_matters: Batch size is a direct memory-scaling factor for CNN workloads.

finding: CNN activation memory grows strongly with image resolution.
evidence: At batch size 1, increasing image size from 64 to 384 increased analytical activation memory by 35.98x.
why_it_matters: CNN feature maps depend on spatial dimensions, so higher image resolution increases memory sharply.

finding: CNN parameter memory is small compared with activation memory for larger inputs.
evidence: SimpleCNN fp32 parameter memory is only 0.3606 MB, while activation memory grows with image size and batch size.
why_it_matters: For CNN inference, activations can dominate memory even when parameter count is small.

finding: CNN memory estimation needs image-resolution-aware features.
evidence: Activation memory changes with H x W feature-map dimensions.
why_it_matters: A GPT-style sequence-length estimator is not enough for CNN-style workloads.

finding: Day 57 focuses on CNN-side scaling only.
evidence: Transformer scaling will be analyzed separately in the next architecture-comparison step.
why_it_matters: Separating CNN and Transformer scaling makes the comparison cleaner.
